en: The Śrīśivapratipādana Stotra (The Hymn of Exposition on the Auspicious Śiva)

Salutations to you, the cause of the creation, preservation, and dissolution of all worlds; salutations to you, the destroyer of the fear of worldly existence for those terrified by *bhava*. Salutations to you, who are to be extolled by the best of the twice-born through the Vedas and Vedāntas; salutations to you who hold a trident in your hand; salutations to you who bear fire in your palm. Salutations to you, the Lord of the universe; salutations to you, the source of the universe; salutations to you, the blue-throated one; salutations to you, who are clothed in an elephant hide.
Salutations to you who are the form of the Moon; salutations to you who are the embodiment of the Sun. Salutations to you who are the form of Fire; salutations to you who are the embodiment of Water.

(4) Salutations to you who are the form of Earth; salutations to you who are the embodiment of Wind. Salutations to you who are the form of Space; salutations indeed to you whose form is the Self. (5) Salutations to you who are the form of Truth; salutations to you who are the embodiment of Truth. Salutations to you who are the form of Bliss; salutations to you who are the embodiment of Bliss. (6)

Salutations to you who are the perfect form; salutations to you who possess the perfect form. Salutations to you who are the form of Brahman; salutations to you who possess the form of Brahman. (7) Salutations to you who are the form of the individual soul; salutations to you who possess the form of the individual soul. Salutations to you who are the manifest form; salutations to you who possess the manifest form. (8) Salutations to you who are the form of sound; salutations to you who possess the form of sound. Salutations to you who are the form of touch; salutations to you who possess the form of touch. (9)

Salutations to you who are the form of form; salutations to you who possess the form of form. Salutations to you who are the essence of taste; salutations to you who possess the essence of taste. 10 Salutations to you who are the essence of smell; salutations to you who possess the essence of smell. Salutations to you who are the form of the body; salutations to you who possess the form of the body. 11 Salutations to you who are the form of life-breath; salutations to you who possess the form of life-breath. Salutations to you who are the form of hearing; salutations to you who possess the form of hearing. 12

Salutations to you whose nature is the skin; salutations to you who possess the form of the skin. Salutations to you whose nature is sight; salutations to you who possess the form of sight. (13) Salutations to you whose nature is taste; salutations to you who possess the form of taste. Salutations to you whose nature is the sense of smell; salutations to you who possess the form of the sense of smell. (14) Salutations to you whose nature is the feet; salutations to you who possess the form of the feet. Salutations to you whose nature is the hands; salutations to you who possess the form of the hands. (15)

Salutations to you whose nature is speech, salutations to you who possess the form of speech; salutations to you whose form is the *liṅga*, salutations to you who possess the form of the *liṅga*. (16) Salutations to you whose form is wind, salutations to you who possess the form of wind; salutations to you whose form is consciousness, salutations to you who possess the form of consciousness.

(17) Salutations to you whose form is the mother, salutations to you who possess the form of the mother; salutations to you whose form is the measure (*māna*), salutations to you who possess the form of the measure. (18)

Salutations to you whose form is the object of knowledge; salutations to you who possess the form of the object of knowledge. Salutations to you whose form is the act of measurement; salutations to you who possess the form of the act of measurement.
(19) Protect me, protect me, O Great God! Forgive me, O Abode of Compassion! O Brahman, seated within the hearts of devotees, whose nature is that of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva!

(20) Having offered praise and prostrated themselves like a staff upon the ground, Sūta, Brahmā, and the others—those gods who had reached the further shore of devotion—became absorbed in the Supreme Lord. (21)
Thus ends the hymn in praise of Śiva from the dialogue between Nandīśvara and Viṣṇu in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa.
